items.title: Custo de violação de dados bate recorde no Brasil e chega a R$ 7,44 milhões
items.pt:
O custo médio de uma violação de dados no Brasil atingiu R$ 7,44 milhões em 2026. É o que mostra o estudo estudo Cost of a Data Breach 2026 da IBM, revelado nesta quinta-feira (15).
A quantia é relacionada aos custos de recuperação de ataques, que envolvem a contratação de especialistas para investigar o incidente, conter danos e restabelecer serviços, além de eventuais multas e sanções.

items.title: Use It or Lose It: 6 Smart Ways to Spend Leftover Training Budget Before Year-End
items.pt:
What is a "Use-It-or-Lose-It" Training Budget?


A use-it-or-lose-it training budget is money set aside for employee training that must be spent before your fiscal year ends. 

Unused training funds usually don't roll over, they return to the general corporate pool and directly shape next year’s allocation. Depending on your company's fiscal calendar, that deadline may be December 31, March 31, or June 30.

items.title: CommerceGen-Studio: An End-to-End Framework for Commercial-Grade Main-Image Generation
items.pt: We present CommerceGen-Studio, an end-to-end framework for generating commercial-grade main images for e-commerce Stock Keeping Units (SKUs). Our framework is organized along a three-stage pipeline of information extraction, semantic rewriting, and multi-condition generation: Prompt-Eval-Refine-Loop Agent (PERL-Agent) distills heterogeneous SKU metadata into concise selling-point text lists through an iterative closed loop of VLM and LLM roles scored by a reference-free rubric. Layout Thinker Op

items.title: DynThinker: Unifying Static 3D and Dynamic 4D Spatial Reasoning
items.pt: Achieving general spatial intelligence requires a unified understanding of both static 3D and dynamic 4D. However, we find that existing models struggle to excel at both: 3D post-training can weaken dynamic understanding, while 4D-specialized models often lack strong static 3D reasoning. items.title: Co-Evolving Acting and Forecasting for Language Agents
items.pt: Training language agents is bottlenecked by the high cost of long-horizon rollouts, yet standard agentic reinforcement learning (RL) learns only from a terminal scalar reward, leaving the supervision in intermediate steps largely unused. Prior work exploits this supervision through value targets that estimate per-step success probabilities or observation targets that fit environment response. Both are hard to construct well: (1) value targets come from the same single scalar signal for each step
